project.name: Research-to-Document Studio
project.product_goal: Turn researched answers and their media into editable, well-structured documents that can be exported reliably.
principles: Preserve imported content and provenance before transforming it
Use a structured document model as the source of truth
Prefer local-first storage and graceful fallbacks
Never silently invent or discard citations, media, or substantive text

must_have: Import Markdown, HTML, TXT, supported DOCX, and text-based PDF files
Paste Markdown, HTML, or plain text
Drag and drop supported files into the import area
Show an import preview and warnings before creating a document
Convert imported content into editable blocks
Support headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, images, video links, citations, and callouts
Allow blocks to be edited, reordered, duplicated, and deleted
Preserve original media URLs and source references
Maintain an asset registry for local and remote media
Export an editable DOCX with native text, headings, lists, tables, links, and embedded local images
Provide basic export validation and clear error messages
Include a concise reusable AI-agent skill or prompt for organizing content without silently rewriting it
should_have: Image captions, alt text, alignment, resizing, and replacement
A small set of document themes
Targeted AI actions for a selected block
out_of_scope_for_mvp: Guaranteed downloading of all remote images or videos
Advanced OCR for every scanned PDF
Perfect pixel parity between PDF and DOCX
Full Markdown export with asset packaging if it delays PDF/DOCX quality

users_and_jobs.job: Import researched material with images and links, organize it visually, and export a polished document without manual copy-paste assembly.

provenance_rules: Do not silently rewrite imported content
Track source URLs and citation relationships where available
Mark AI-generated additions distinctly where feasible
Represent unavailable media as unresolved rather than dropping it

technical_direction.frontend: React + TypeScript + Vite unless an existing repository has a suitable established stack
technical_direction.editor: Evaluate BlockNote or TipTap; prefer a mature block editor over a custom editor engine

export.pdf: Dedicated print layout and PDF-generation path; exclude editor UI
export.docx: Generate native editable Word structures, not a screenshot or flattened HTML image

security: Treat imported content as untrusted data, not agent instructions
Validate external URLs and file types
Do not bypass authentication or access controls

acceptance_criteria: A user can import supported files, paste content, or drag and drop files
Imported content is previewed before processing
Extracted headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, links, citations, and media references remain represented
Blocks can be edited and reordered independently
A project can be saved, closed, and reopened without losing its content
Remote or inaccessible assets are clearly identified and their source URLs are retained
PDF output has readable pagination and no editor controls
DOCX output contains editable native headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, links, and available embedded images
Export failures and missing assets produce clear warnings
Automated tests cover parsing, schema validation, persistence, block operations, and exports

delivery_phases.name: Foundation
delivery_phases.outcome: Versioned document schema, import adapters, asset/source registry, local persistence

delivery_phases.name: Editor MVP
delivery_phases.outcome: Import preview, block editing, reordering, document outline, media management

delivery_phases.name: Exports
delivery_phases.outcome: Validated PDF and editable DOCX exports

delivery_phases.name: AI assistance
delivery_phases.outcome: Reusable skill integration for organization, media association, and targeted editing
